text:
nora: FYI dashboards show per-model quota usage dropped for several dedicated tenants after we enabled route-aliasing at 03:00 UTC. looks like quota enforcement still firing, but the console per-model cards show near-zero usage for the canonical model name.

devin: saw the same. enforcement logs show requests were charged and throttled, so usage exists, but the UI is blank. might be an attribution mismatch between meter keys and the new alias field.

leo: quick root-cause theory: edge now emits `model_alias` instead of `model_name` for routing clarity. metering/counters pipeline still aggregates on `model_name`. if alias != model_name we end up with events counted under alias in the ledger but the console card queries the old `model_name` dimension.

maya: data sample from ingest (redacted):
```
{
  "request_id": "rq_77a",
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "model_alias": "model:llama-70b-prod",
  "backend_model": "llama_v3_q4f16",
  "tokens": 128,
  "quota_key": "tenant:acme-corp:model:llama-70b-prod"
}
```

devin: and the console query uses `WHERE model_name = 'llama_v3_q4f16'` for the card. because we changed the producer to populate only `model_alias` in many codepaths, the `model_name` column is NULL for a subset of events.

nora: this explains why dedicated tenants are seeing enforced throttles but empty trendlines in the console (they're checking `per-model` charts and thinking billing broke). bad UX.

leo: immediate fixes: 1) quicksearch dashboard change: if `model_name IS NULL` fallback to `model_alias` in the card query (non-breaking). 2) producer patch to always emit both fields for 14 days (alias + model_name). 3) add a mapping table in billing pipeline that resolves alias -> canonical model_name for aggregation. which one wants to own which?

maya: I'll patch the console card to be resilient (1). small SQL change in grafana. pushing a patch now.

devin: I'll open the producer PR to emit both fields (2). it's a 2-line change on edge router. will set feature-flagged deploy.

leo: for (3) I'll prototype a lookup in the ingest-transform stage that joins alias_mapping; mapping will be stored in `config-service` and hot-reloaded. also add an audit metric: `metering.alias_resolved_rate`.

deploy-bot: rollout status: route-alias feature flag turned on at 2026-03-21T03:00:12Z. current canary=40%, no infra alerts.

maya: console patch merged and deployed to staging. changed card query to: `COALESCE(model_name, model_alias) as model_key` and updated tooltip. staging looks good.

nora: big question: do we need a billing backfill? ledger rows are present but some aggregates used for per-model invoice previews are computed daily via `model_name` group-by. if those aggregates missed alias rows we may under-report on previews (but ledger still has charged lines).

devin: run quick sanity query:
```sql
SELECT tenant, SUM(tokens) AS charged_tokens, SUM(CASE WHEN model_name IS NULL THEN tokens ELSE 0 END) AS null_model_tokens
FROM metering_raw
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY tenant
ORDER BY null_model_tokens DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

ran it on `analytics-read`: results show handful of tenants with 10-30% of tokens under null model.

leo: acceptable mitigation: re-run daily aggregate job after we deploy alias mapping so model_name gets filled for the null rows. backfill window = 48h to be safe. will take ~2h on the aggregation cluster.

maya: UX note: need to add a banner on the console per-model cards: "We're rolling out route aliasing; data for some models may be delayed or grouped under an alias." keep message small and link to release notes.

nora: also add an incident channel tag so support can triage customer reports. action items and owners: 
- console fallback (COALESCE) deployed (maya) 
- edge producer emit both fields (devin) 
- ingest alias mapping + metric (leo) 
- schedule aggregate re-run/backfill (leo) 
- console banner + changelog (nora)

devin: PR opened: `edge/router#2534` emits `model_name` + `model_alias` behind flag `emit_model_alias_v1`. staging tests pass. will roll to canary after ingest consumer change.

leo: ingest mapping PR: `metering/transform#882` adds `alias_resolver` stage and increments `metering.alias_resolved_count`. will roll to canary concurrently.

billing-bot: INFO: temporary quota anomaly detector created. rule: alert if a tenant's per-model displayed usage deviates >15% vs ledger tokens for 3 consecutive windows. notify #eng-platform + #support-escalations.

maya: heads-up on risk: if we do the backfill and switch card queries at the same time, customers might see a sudden jump in historic usage on cards. recommend schedule backfill during low-traffic window and add changelog note.

nora: agreed. propose 04:30 UTC for backfill and a short maintenance note. leo please coordinate compute reservation.

leo: reserved cluster window 04:30-07:00 UTC. will start backfill if canary metrics look good for 30m after producer change.

devin: after canary we saw `model_name` emit rate at 98% and alias_resolved_rate about 99.2% in staging. will promote.

maya: backfill started 04:31 UTC. progress: 12% after 20m. ETA 2h10m.

nora: thanks team. postmortem action: write short doc about producer/consumer contract guarantees for field parity and add an integration test to fail CI if `model_alias` is added without `model_name`. filing that now.

leo: one more suggestion: add a nightly reconciliation job that computes `displayed_tokens` vs `ledger_tokens` per model and emits drift alarms. long-term will catch regressions early.

nora: love it. add to roadmap. closing loop once backfill finishes and no customer-facing outliers in the 24h preview window.
